answer: Sparrow-Trellis Consistency Rule An agent must maintain identical behavioral patterns across two consecutive epochs on a shared activity graph. If deviations exceed a threshold—such as sudden shifts in message timing, routing paths, or interaction frequency—the agent is flagged. Each identity must anchor its actions to a persistent node within a decentralized trellis structure that logs sequence-based behavioral fingerprints. To register or persist, each agent must deposit one walnut-sized cryptographic commitment per epoch, verifiable via zero-knowledge proofs tied to historical behavior.
